title: UnitedHealth Sues Over 2027 Medicare Advantage Star Ratings, Becoming at Least the 15th Plan to Challenge CMS - Medical Daily

 Vitality How to Live Better, Longer
 Frequent Night Shift Workers Had Slightly Thicker Heart Walls and Smaller Chambers in MRI Study of 42,671 Adults 
 A cardiac MRI study of 42,671 UK adults found frequent night shift workers had slightly thicker heart walls and smaller chambers, without a significant difference in pumping ability. 
 Several Short Brisk Walks a Day Controlled Blood Sugar Better Than One Long Walk in Small Trial 
 In a six-week randomized trial of 30 sedentary adults, several short brisk walks improved blood sugar control more than one continuous 45-minute walk, though larger studies are needed. 
 Migraine and Smoking Together Tied to 3.6 Times the Risk of Early Ischemic Stroke in Danish Mothers 
 Un estudio observacional realizado en casi 1,7 millones de madres danesas relacionó la migraña y el tabaquismo con un mayor riesgo de ictus isquémico antes de los 60 años, sin demostrar causalidad. 
 Federal Workers Still Cannot Buy Long-Term Care Insurance Through OPM as Application Freeze Is Extended Into Late 2028 
 OPM extended its suspension of new Federal Long Term Care Insurance Program applications through at least December 2028, leaving current enrollees covered but unable to increase benefits. 
 Mental Health 
 A Man's Decade of Urges to Bite Arteries and Drink Blood Was Traced to Psychosis 
 A 28-year-old man's decade of urges to drink blood occurred alongside hallucinations and delusions. Doctors concluded the symptoms reflected schizoaffective disorder, not a separate Renfield syndrome diagnosis. 
 Webster Groves Hospital Adds 65 Crisis Beds in December for St. Louis Children Facing Mental Health Emergencies 
 A new Webster Groves hospital is set to add 77 beds and outpatient programs for children and teens with mental health conditions, addressing a shortage across the St. Louis region. 
 Teens Who Drink Heavily or Use Cannabis in More Ways Had Higher Depression Odds in Survey of 9,817 
 A survey of 9,817 U.S. teens found heavier drinking and using cannabis in multiple ways were associated with higher odds of major depression, while researchers cautioned that cause and effect remain unclear. 
 Young Adults With Depression or Anxiety Who Cut Back on Social Media Were More Likely to Improve 
 A study of 2,358 young adults found that those with elevated depression or anxiety symptoms who reduced social media checks were more likely to improve later, though causation remains unproven. 
 Innovation 
 Experimental KRAS G12D Degrader Plus Chemotherapy Shrinks Tumors in 6 of 7 Assessed Pancreatic Cancer Patients 
 PT0253 plus modified FOLFIRINOX shrank tumors in six of seven assessable patients with newly treated metastatic pancreatic cancer, according to preliminary Phase 1 results without a comparison group. 
 Rezatapopt Pill Shrank Tumors in 48% of Women With Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer 
 Rezatapopt shrank tumors in 48% of 65 women with platinum-resistant or refractory ovarian cancer and a TP53 Y220C mutation, but the single-arm trial cannot establish survival benefits. 
 Medicare Could Cover Alzheimer's Blood Screening Tests From 2028 Under ASAP Act as Current Congress Nears Its End 
 The bipartisan ASAP Act could allow Medicare to cover FDA-approved or cleared blood tests for early Alzheimer's detection starting in 2028, if Congress passes it. 
 Getting Alzheimer's Gene Results Online Matched Clinician Video Visits on Anxiety in Trial of 651 Older Adults 
 A randomized trial of 651 older adults found that receiving APOE Alzheimer's gene results online produced similar anxiety and distress outcomes to clinician-led video visits, though satisfaction was lower.

 USDA Lists E. Coli O157 Outbreak With Ground Beef as Suspected Source but Releases No Case Count 
 USDA's FSIS has listed an active E. coli O157:H7 investigation involving suspected ground beef, but has released no case count, affected states, recall or named product. 
 Lunch Box Breakfast Biscuits Sold in Convenience Stores, Vending Machines and Prison Canteens Recalled Over Listeria Risk 
 Grand Strand Sandwich Company recalled four Lunch Box breakfast biscuit products sold in three states because of possible Listeria contamination. Consumers should check UPCs and date codes before discarding them. 
 Two Lesser-Known Forever Chemicals Tied to Up to 2.5 Times the Odds of Liver Cancer in USC Study 
 A USC study of 446 people found that higher blood levels of PFHpA and PFNA were associated with increased odds of liver cancer, but did not prove causation. 
 Labor Department Plan Would End Green Card Fast Track for Foreign Nurses as Hospitals Warn of Shortages 
 A Labor Department proposal would eliminate Schedule A, forcing employers sponsoring foreign nurses and physical therapists to use the longer PERM process amid warnings of staffing shortages, especially in rural areas.

 UnitedHealth Sues Over 2027 Medicare Advantage Star Ratings, Becoming at Least the 15th Plan to Challenge CMS
 Published Nov 20, 2026 10:54 PM EST 
 By
 Elena Vega 
 Kampus Production | Pexels 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on WhatsApp 
 Update Note: This article reports new information involving lawsuits over 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings following MedicalDaily's earlier coverage. The newest information comes from STAT, Reuters, and Law360 reports published Nov. 20, 2026.
 UnitedHealth Group has sued the federal government over its lowered 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings, making it at least the 15th Medicare Advantage plan to challenge how the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services calculated this year's scores, STAT reported Nov. 20.
 UnitedHealth is the nation's largest Medicare Advantage insurer, covering more than 9 million people, according to STAT. Its suit asks a federal court in Georgia to vacate dozens of its 2027 ratings, Law360 reported .
 For UnitedHealthcare members , the suit lands with open enrollment ending Dec. 7 . Star ratings are among the first things seniors see when they compare plans, and the largest insurer is now telling a court that its own ratings understate its quality.
 The Largest Insurer Joins the Litigation
 In its complaint, filed in federal court in Brunswick, Georgia, UnitedHealth said CMS improperly used 26 measures to calculate ratings for 45 contracts, either because the agency lacked legal authority, failed to give the company a chance to object, or both, Reuters reported . The company said correct calculations would raise those contracts by at least half a star and by as much as a star and a half. Those are UnitedHealth's claims and have not been tested in court.
 The Georgia venue is notable. In May, a federal judge in the same court ruled that CMS had improperly used 20 measures in calculating Clover Health's 2026 rating, and that decision has become the foundation for most of the new lawsuits. CVS Health's suit over its Aetna plans was also filed in that court.
 Since MedicalDaily's last tally of 11 lawsuits , Molina Healthcare, UPMC Health Plan, and Point32Health, the parent of Tufts Health Plan and Harvard Pilgrim, have also sued, according to a Becker's Payer Issues tracker . Molina says about $140 million in 2028 bonus payments and rebates is at stake, UPMC about $41 million, and Point32Health about $41.4 million.
 UnitedHealth has a track record in this fight. It won a 2024 lawsuit in Texas over a single disputed customer-service test call, and CMS later dropped its appeal.
 Bonus Dollars Tied to the Four-Star Line
 CMS rates Medicare Advantage contracts from 1 to 5 stars using measures that include preventive screenings, chronic disease care, medication adherence, member surveys, and customer service. Plans with at least 4 stars earn quality bonus payments, and higher ratings also raise the rebates plans can use for extra benefits.
 The 2027 ratings, released Oct. 8, appear on Medicare Plan Finder and affect payments in 2028, according to CMS . Insurers argue that CMS's measurement is inconsistent and is pushing their scores below the bonus line, STAT reported.
 The money involved is large. Writing in Health Affairs , leaders of SCAN Health Plan, which has brought its own star ratings suits, said the Clover ruling produced a half-star swing worth roughly $120 million to a single plan.
 That money comes from Medicare's trust funds. If insurers win, Medicare spends more, and plans may use the money for richer benefits. If CMS prevails, plans may trim extras to absorb lost revenue. Both outcomes involve trade-offs for taxpayers and enrollees.
 Details Still Missing From Public Reports
 Several key facts have not been reported. UnitedHealth's dollar estimate of lost bonuses was not made public in the coverage reviewed, and it is not clear which states or plan names the 45 contracts cover.
 CMS declined to comment. No court has ruled on UnitedHealth's 2027 claims, and CMS is appealing the Clover decision.
 The figures for UnitedHealth's size also differ by source. STAT put coverage at more than 9 million people, while Reuters reported that the company serves 7.61 million Medicare Advantage patients, a difference that may reflect how plan types are counted.
 The lawsuits also do not answer whether the star system accurately measures quality. CMS's 2027 Medicare Advantage rule removes 11 measures the agency described as administrative or lacking meaningful variation, mostly starting with the 2029 ratings.
 The timing of any ruling is unknown. A decision on UnitedHealth's 2027 claims could come after open enrollment closes, too late to change what members see on Plan Finder this fall. A later win for the company would mainly affect 2028 bonus payments and the extra benefits plans designed for that year.
 For UnitedHealthcare members, that means the practical choice this season rests on what plans offer for 2027, not on how the lawsuit turns out.
 Choices for UnitedHealthcare Members Before December 7
 The lawsuit does not change 2027 benefits. Premiums, copays, and extra benefits for next year were set months ago, and they will not change mid-year because of a court case.
 Members comparing plans can treat star ratings as one guide while checking doctor and hospital networks, drug coverage, and total yearly costs, including the out-of-pocket maximum. Plan Finder shows scores on individual measures, such as care coordination or drug plan service, which may matter more to a given person than the overall number.
 Free, unbiased help is available through each state's State Health Insurance Assistance Program and at 1-800-MEDICARE. People already in Medicare Advantage can make one change between Jan. 1 and March 31.
 MedicalDaily will report court rulings, any change to UnitedHealth's 2027 ratings, and the outcome of CMS's Clover appeal.

 Key Questions Answered
 What did UnitedHealth do? It sued CMS over its 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings, becoming at least the 15th plan to do so.
 What does it claim? That CMS improperly used 26 measures to rate 45 contracts, without legal authority, without proper notice, or both.
 Will my UnitedHealthcare benefits change in 2027? No. Benefits for 2027 are already set.
 Where was the suit filed? In federal court in Brunswick, Georgia.
 Has any court ruled on UnitedHealth's 2027 claims? No. The case is pending.
 When does open enrollment end? Dec. 7, 2026. Medicare Advantage members can make one more change from Jan. 1 to March 31.
